instruction: Configure nginx with a basic HTTP virtual host for example.com that serves static files from /var/www/html on port 80.
Set up an nginx server block that listens on port 8080 for the hostname dashboard.internal and serves files from /srv/dashboard.
Make nginx close the connection with code 444 for every request that does not match a configured server_name on port 80.
Configure two virtual hosts, shop.example.com and blog.example.com, on port 80 with separate document roots.
Create an nginx server block on port 3000 that only answers to the hostname grafana.monitoring and serves /usr/share/grafana/public.
Serve the site in /opt/site so directory requests try home.html first, then index.html, and return 404 when the file does not exist.
Configure nginx to reject request bodies larger than 2 MB for the upload service at upload.example.com on port 80.
Tune nginx for high-throughput static delivery on assets.example.com by enabling sendfile, TCP nopush and a 65 second keepalive timeout.
Serve the French site in /var/www/fr and declare charset utf-8 on every response for www.exemple.fr.
Configure custom error pages so 404 responses show /404.html and 502, 503 or 504 responses show /50x.html.
Configure a default server on port 80 that serves a placeholder landing page from /var/www/default for any unknown Host header.
Write a server block that responds to both example.org and www.example.org on port 80 using the document root /var/www/example-org.
Add a server block for a Node.js app on port 8000 with server_name app.local that writes its own access and error logs.
Hide the nginx version number in response headers and error pages for the site legacy.example.net.
Serve the same site on both port 80 and port 8080 with a single server block for www.same-site.io.
Write a server block that matches only the exact hostname old.example.com with no wildcards, serving /var/www/old.
Configure nginx to buffer client bodies up to 64k and time out slow clients after 30 seconds on form.example.com.
Create a minimal health-check endpoint that answers 200 OK without reading any file from disk for the load balancer on port 80.
Configure nginx to listen only on IPv6 port 80 for the host v6.example.com.
Turn off absolute redirects for www.behind-lb.example so nginx issues relative Location headers when it runs behind a load balancer.
